title: Scenes have access to Scene Unique Nodes from their owner's scene
body: ### Tested versions v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] - has issue v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1] - has issue v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee] - has issue v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8] - has issue v4.3.dev6.official [64520fe67] - has issue v4.3.dev5.official [c9c17d6ca] - does NOT have issue v4.3.dev4.official [df78c0636] - does NOT have issue v4.3.dev3.official [36e943b6b] - does NOT have issue v4.2.2.stable.official [15073afe3] - does NOT have issue v4.2.1.stable.official [b09f793f5] - does NOT have issue v4.2.stable.official [46dc27791] - does NOT have issue v4.1.stable.official [970459615] - does NOT have issue v4.0.1.stable.official [cacf49999] - does NOT have issue v4.0.stable.official [92bee43ad] - does NOT have issue ### System information Godot v4.6.stable - Linux Mint 22.1 ### Issue description I had a confusing bug in my project where a nested scene accidentally retrieved a node from its owner's scene, using the Scene Unique Nodes feature. Both nodes happened to have the same name. Based on my understanding of this feature, it seems to be an error. I made a MRP that attempts to get unique nodes from other scenes from different positions in the Scene Tree hierarchy. Here are its results from v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439]: I tested various releases and it seems that this became possible in v4.3.dev6.official [64520fe67]. Output from v4.3.dev5.official [c9c17d6ca] and earlier works as expected: ### Steps to reproduce - Create and save Scene A. - Add a node to Scene A with a unique node name. - Create and save Scene B with a script on its root node. - Instantiate Scene B inside of Scene A. - From Scene B's root node script, attempt to access the unique node from Scene A. To use the MRP: open the project and run it with F5, check the output window. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [unique_node_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25330256/unique_node_mrp.zip)
